habitat: Lowland evergreen forest; secondary growth; mangroves; peatswamp forest; and wet areas
story: Few birds capture the imagination quite like the White Collared Blackbird (Pellorneum rostratum). As a member of the Pellorneidae family, it has carved out a unique niche in Lowland evergreen forest; secondary growth; mangroves; peatswamp forest; and wet areas. Its conservation status is Near Threatened (NT), a classification that drives crucial research and protection efforts. The White Collared Blackbird's presence is a vital sign of its ecosystem's health, making its preservation a priority. This poster is a tribute to the White Collared Blackbird, celebrating its role in the natural world and inspiring a deeper appreciation for biodiversity.
